fuel_basis: Not established in any public source found. The operator describes the facility design as including "self-contained power generation" but does not name a fuel (gas turbine/genset vs. diesel) or equipment for that on-site power generation.
captive_summary: UTM Offshore's own project description (NNPC 20%-stake announcement, 25 Jul 2023) lists "self-contained power generation" as one of the FLNG facility's design components, alongside a turret mooring system, gas pretreatment modules, LNG production modules, living quarters, and utilities/storage/offloading. No MW figure, turbine/generator model, or explicit fuel type is disclosed in any public source found. The project is pre-FID (FEED substantially complete since 2023; 15-year gas supply agreement signed ~7 Jul 2026; FID reportedly targeted later in 2026), so detailed engineering specifications for the power system are not yet public.
confirmed_how: UTM Offshore Limited's own press release (utmoffshore.com, 25 Jul 2023, 'NNPC Takes 20% Stake in UTM FLNG Project') states the FLNG facility 'comprises a turret mooring system, gas pretreatment modules, LNG production modules, living quarters, self-contained power generation, and utilities alongside storage and offloading.' This confirms the DESIGN includes on-site power generation, but no other public source checked — UTM Offshore's own FLNG service page (utmoffshore.com/flng/), its full press archive, the JGC/Technip Energies/KBR FEED-award coverage (aecweek.com, JGC's own 18 Nov 2022 press release), or business/trade press on the July 2026 gas supply agreement (Reuters, BusinessDay, InvestorsKing, energychamber.org, infradialogue.com) — names a fuel type, MW rating, or equipment model for that power generation. No environmental/regulatory filing was found publicly describing the power system; the only Nigerian regulatory milestone found is NMDPRA's Sept 2024 'License to Construct,' which is a construction authorization, not a technical EIA/permit with equipment detail. Multiple search engines were used to attempt corroboration (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Marginalia); most returned bot-challenge pages or irrelevant results for this query, so a second independent source could not be obtained despite a genuine search.
